rv.q: Co-directors and choreographers Lucy Ireland and Jim Manganello provide a superbly sharp staging. Designer Anna Yates delivers a sterile square, over which a digital counter clocks ever upwards – 3,097, 4,231, 5,824 – and in front of which a bank of boxy monitors live-streams every move of the room’s inhabitant.
It results in a highly theatrical piece of theatre, where the vision is often the medium through which the narrative is driven.
So much of the production is so impressive that it is a shame that it wobbles a little towards the end, but the overall effect is still very fine.
Shotput Theatre ’s production blends the physical, the distorted and the hope we have as humanity into a haunting exploration of connection and survival.

cn.t: Walsh's dystopian drama about isolation delivers rare intensity through its stark premise of a woman trapped in a state-controlled tower. Critics find the production compelling, though the bleak subject matter proves emotionally draining.
